chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'The guardianship (wilayah) is for the one who emancipates.'

key_terms.الْوَلَاءُ: Guardianship or manumission bond; the legal relationship between a master and a freed slave.

ai.seo_question: Who has the right of guardianship over a freed slave according to the Prophet?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) via the Prophet (SAW), establishes 'al-wala' as the right of the manumitter, a principle central to Shia and Sunni jurisprudence regarding inheritance and social bonds. It clarifies that this guardianship is not merely social but carries legal weight, particularly in determining who inherits from the freed slave if they die without direct heirs. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of the Kufan school of hadith, with scholars like Hammad ibn Uthman and Muhammad ibn Muslim serving as key transmitters.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby and Muhammad Bin Muslim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The Prophet<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘The guardianship is for the one who emancipates (frees)’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy and Muhammad ibn Muslim who has narrated the following: “Abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Holy Prophet, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause,
has said, ‘Guardianship rests in favor of one who sets one free.’”
